To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified the ER proteins VAPA and VapB as proteins copurifing with the plasma membrane Kv2.1 channel and that expression of Kv21 recruits VAPs and organizes ER-PM junction in brain neurons and in other mammalian cells.
we identified a protein that is crucial to the formation of ER-PM contacts in mammalian brain neurons and that this interaction depends on the Kv2.1 PM protein.
VAPs are recruited to ER-PM contact sites in brain neurons through their association with the Kv2 ion channel and that this association depends on a noncanonical FFAT motif in Kv2.1.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanism of how a voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channel localizes to ER-PM membrane contact sites in mammalian neurons and how this localization affects ER-PM junction formation and function.
the identification and characterization of ER-PM contact sites in mammalian neurons.
the Kv2.1 channel and its role in organizing ER-PM junctional complexes in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study identified the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) protein VAPs as proteins copurify with the plasma membrane potassium (K+) channel Kv2.1.

our study identified the resident ER proteins VAPA and VAB as proteins copurify with the PM ion channel Kv2.1, and that Kv2. channels recruit VAPs and VAPs are required for Kv2 channel clustering at ER-PM contacts in neurons.

we identified VAPA and VBP as proteins that associate with Kv2.2 and Kv2.3 at ER-PM contact sites in brain neurons and that this association is mediated by a novel noncanonical phosphorylation dependent FFAT motif in Kv2 channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Kv2.2 channels localize to ER-PM contacts in neurons through their interactions with the VAPs.
Kv2. channels organize ER-PM contacts through their association with VAPs.
Kv2.2.1 localizing to the PM can recruit ER proteins to the PM and affect their function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ER-PM junction organization in mammalian brain neurons involves the interaction of the Kv2.1 PM ion channel with the ER-resident VAPA and VABP proteins.
Kv2.2 and Kv2.3 channels are also capable of recruiting VAPs to the PM.
